title: Use work-energy to solve motion
target: Choose work-energy when force and displacement are known.
criteria: Check whether the result is physically possible.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A crate slides horizontally. A rope pulls forward, friction acts backward, and gravity and normal forces are vertical. Which forces do nonzero work in this model?
options: All four do equal positive work.
No force can do work on a sliding object.
cpa.guide: Vertical forces are perpendicular to displacement; forward and backward components do work.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A student calculates net work using only a drive force and ignores a stated opposing friction force. What correction is needed?
options: Add friction’s magnitude as positive work.
Include friction’s negative work in the sum.
cpa.guide: Net work requires every force’s signed contribution over the same displacement.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: A cart has 28 J of kinetic energy. The net work over an interval is −10 J. What is final kinetic energy?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 2 kg cart’s speed increases from 3 to 5 m/s. What net work was done?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A moving cart has 15 J of kinetic energy. A proposed calculation gives final kinetic energy −5 J. What does that indicate?
options: The result is valid if the cart moves left.
The assumed motion interval or model is invalid; kinetic energy cannot be negative.
Negative kinetic energy means ordinary motion in the negative direction.
cpa.guide: For ordinary positive mass, ½mv² ≥ 0; examine whether stopping occurs before the assumed interval ends.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.

cpa.prompt: An object starts with 27 J of kinetic energy. A constant 9 N opposing force is the only force doing work. How far does it move before stopping?
cpa.guide: To stop, negative work must be −27 J: −9d = −27 gives d = 3 m.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.
